This cold start run was conducted over multiple days at a reduced heating rate. The blue and green lines represent the HTF temperature at the inlet and outlet of TES, respectively during the heating operation. The orange line indicates the bulk sulfur temperature. The repeated decreases in sulfur temperature correspond to heat loss during daily non-operational periods, typically around 12 -14 hours. A larger drop in the sulfur temperature observed in Figure 45 occurred during the weekend when the system remained idle for an extended duration. During this cold startup run, the system was charged at an average heat input rate of 20–30 kW. While the system is designed for a maximum charging rate of 100 kW, a lower and controlled heat input was used in this test to ensure safe startup conditions and to verify system integrity during initial operation.
